title: Infra GPU Fleet, Cloud Accounts & IaC CI/CD Runbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
========
This document is the canonical infra runbook for provisioning and operating Redwood's GPU fleet, associated cloud accounts & networking, and the Terraform/CI-CD modules and pipelines we use to manage them. It covers: capacity planning, IaC module patterns, CI/CD build & promotion flows, emergency and regular runbook procedures, ownership, SLOs, and common troubleshooting commands.

Audience
--------
- Infra engineers and oncall SREs
- Platform and runtime engineers who request fleet capacity or network changes
- Solutions engineers onboarding Dedicated/Private customers requiring private VPC peering and account setup

High-level responsibilities
---------------------------
- infra-engineering: maintain IaC modules, CI/CD pipelines, capacity forecasting, and day-2 ops runbooks.
- cloud-ops: account lifecycle, billing alerts, org-level networking controls.
- runtime-team: scheduling, kernel selection, and model-serving capacity requests.

Key services & components
-------------------------
- GPU Fleet (service name: gpu-pool-manager): Kubernetes node pools with GPU nodegroups (NVIDIA A100 / H100), autoscaler, and capacity allocator.
- Accounts service (service name: cloud-accounts): account provisioning via Organization API, account IAM baseline, and VPC templates.
- IaC registry (terraform modules): modules/compute/gpu-nodegroup, modules/network/vpc-peering, modules/accounts/account-bootstrap.
- CI/CD (service name: infra-pipeline): GitHub Actions / CircleCI pipelines that run plan/apply, module tests, and promotion gates.

SLOs & operational thresholds
----------------------------
- Provisioning time: 95th percentile for new nodegroup creation <= 30 minutes (target).
- Scale-up time (existing nodegroup): 90th percentile <= 6 minutes.
- Autorepair success rate: >= 99.5% per month.
- Alerting thresholds:
  - GPU utilization (cluster avg) > 80% for 10m -> paged to infra oncall.
  - Nodegroup unready count > 3 for 5m -> page infra oncall.
  - Billing anomaly: spend delta > 20% forecast -> alert to finance & cloud-ops.

Capacity planning checklist (quarterly)
-------------------------------------
1. Gather usage metrics: token-per-second job counts, average load per model, percentile sequence length.
2. Forecast demand by product team signals (expected feature launches, large enterprise onboards).
3. Run capacity simulation using the perf-suite (runtime bench).
4. Create purchase or cloud quota request tickets for extra GPUs or vCPUs.
5. Schedule provisioning windows and coordinate with network/account owners for peering & ACLs.

Terraform / IaC module patterns
-----------------------------
- Module layout (recommended):
  - modules/gpu-nodegroup: takes variables: region, instance_type, desired_capacity, min_capacity, max_capacity, taints, labels, launch_template_id.
  - modules/network/vpc-peering: variables: requester_account_id, accepter_account_id, vpc_cidr, allow_routes_boolean.
  - modules/accounts/account-bootstrap: creates baseline IAM roles, SCPs, logging sinks, and sentinel policies.

- Best practices:
  - Keep modules small and composable.
  - Use a single source-of-truth variables file per environment (env: prod/staging/dev).
  - Avoid hard-coded account IDs in modules; pass them as variables.
  - Tag all resources with: team, owner, cost-center, project, lifecycle.

Example module usage (snippet)
-----------------------------
```hcl
module "gpu_nodegroup_prod" {
  source            = "git::git@github.com:redwood/infra-modules.git//modules/gpu-nodegroup"
  region            = "us-west-2"
  instance_type     = "nvidia-h100-80gb"
  desired_capacity  = 24
  min_capacity      = 4
  max_capacity      = 200
  labels            = { pool = "inference-prod" }
  taints            = [{ key = "dedicated", value = "true", effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" }]
}
```

CI/CD & pipeline flow
---------------------
- Branch strategy: feature branches -> PR to main -> module-level tests run -> staging promotion -> manual gate -> prod apply.
- Stages:
  1. lint (tflint, tfsec)
  2. unit & integration tests (kitchen / terratest)
  3. terraform plan (on PR) with cost estimation step
  4. apply to staging (automated)
  5. canary/prod apply (manual approval)
- Promotion rules: any change that alters instance types, scaling policies, or IAM must include reviewers from runtime-team and security.

Pre-apply checklist (required before prod apply)
------------------------------------------------
- Verify plan: no unexpected resource deletions, no broad IAM policy changes.
- Confirm cloud quotas or purchase orders exist.
- Run perf & smoke tests in staging region.
- Notify runtime-team + oncall window scheduled in PagerDuty.

Runbook: common operational procedures
-------------------------------------
- Scale-up existing nodegroup (fast path):
  1. Confirm desired_capacity in Terraform variables or AWS console.
  2. If using autoscaler, check autoscaler metrics and evictions: kubectl -n kube-system get hpa,pods -o wide
  3. Trigger scale via terraform: terraform workspace select prod && terraform apply -var-file=prod.tfvars -target=module.gpu_nodegroup_prod
  4. Verify new nodes: kubectl get nodes -l "pool=inference-prod"

- Emergency: nodegroup failing to come up (pager flow)
  1. Page infra oncall immediately.
  2. Check provider console for instance lifecycle events (spot interruptions, quota errors).
  3. If quota: open cloud support ticket and trigger emergency capacity fallback (route traffic to dedicated smaller models / lower tiers).
  4. If AMI/kernel issue: revert launch template to previous working version (launch_template_id).
  5. Post-incident: create postmortem and link to this doc.

- Add new cloud account & VPC peering (standard flow):
  1. Create account scaffold using modules/accounts/account-bootstrap via infra-pipeline->apply.
  2. Ensure centralized logging sink is configured (Stackdriver/CloudWatch -> central logging account).
  3. Create VPC in requester account and run modules/network/vpc-peering to the shared-services VPC.
  4. Apply route tables and security groups: restrict CIDR ranges to /28 where possible for admin subnets.
  5. Validate connectivity: run curl/sshd checks from bastion -> private endpoint.

Security & compliance checks
--------------------------
- IAM baseline: MFA enforced for all human users, roles limited to least-privilege.
- KMS keys: all EBS volumes and S3 buckets used by cluster backups must be encrypted with CMKs in customer's key policy.
- Audit logging: resource creation & IAM changes forwarded to security-account logging sink (retention 365 days).
- PRs that change IAM, network peering, or audit configuration must be marked with label `security-review`.

Troubleshooting commands & queries
---------------------------------
- Check node readiness and GPU drivers:
  kubectl describe node <node-name>
  dmesg | grep -i nvidia
  nvidia-smi -L
- List GPU-backed pods and evicted pods: kubectl get pods -A -o wide | grep -i gpu
- Terraform plan diff with cost: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform show -json tfplan | jq '.planned_values'
- Cloud billing query (example GCP BigQuery):
  SELECT service, SUM(cost) FROM `billing.gcp` WHERE usage_start_time >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) GROUP BY service

Ownership & escalation
----------------------
- Primary owners:
  - infra-engineering (primary): #infra-eng Slack channel, infra-oncall@redwood.com
  - cloud-ops (secondary): #cloud-ops Slack channel
- Escalation path:
  1. Oncall engineer -> team lead (if > 30m unresolved)
  2. Team lead -> infra-eng manager & runtime-ops (if > 2 hours)
  3. Exec alert (if customer-facing outage or > 6 hours)

Post-deployment checklist
-------------------------
- Verify monitoring: new nodes show in Grafana dashboards (gpu-utilization, nodecount) and Prometheus metrics are present.
- Confirm cost budgets updated for new capacity.
- Tagging validated across cloud console and cost allocation report.
- Close change ticket and add references to rolling change log.

Appendix: quick links & templates
--------------------------------
- Terraform module repo: git@github.com:redwood/infra-modules.git
- CI/CD pipeline docs: internal:/confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-docs
